newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union chief attacks Socialists job plan.
newsitem.headline: French union chief attacks Socialists job plan.

text.p: The head of the pro-Socialist CFDT, France's largest union, spoke out on Wednesday against one of the opposition party's main election campaign planks -- cutting the work week with no loss in wages.
"A good reduction in hours must guarantee the interests of the company which needs to adjust to changing realities," Nicole Notat, known in union circles as a moderate, told business daily Les Echos.
Without specifically mentioning the Socialists by name, she said parties should "steer clear of the danger" of decreeing an across-the-board reduction in hours without loss of pay.

Socialist Party chief Lionel Jospin has proposed reducing the work week to 35 hours from 39 hours without any drop in pay and made it one of the central plank's in his party's platform for the May/June two-round parliamentary election.

The plan, aimed at reducing France's record 12.8 percent unemployment rate, has been attacked by economists and the ruling centre right as unrealistic as it would boost company costs and lead to possibly more unemployment.

The Socialists have also proposed a government-backed scheme to create 700,000 jobs for young people -- 350,000 in the public sector and 350,000 in the private sector -- and a reform of payroll charges to cut the cost of labour.
Notat said Socialist party should give details of how it would get the private sector to hire 350,000 young people.
Meanwhile, Jospin told France Inter radio that his plan to create 700,000 jobs for young people was based on France's strong economic fundamentals.
"Today inflation is beaten and we have a trade surplus," he said. We have the margin to act," he said.
"The 700,000 jobs would not be right away -- it would be in two years," he said. "I do not want young people to begin their working lives by an experience as traumatic as unemployment.
